Working with @AMD, our models identified up to 14% PPA improvement on flagship GPU IP in less than five months—building on designs AMD’s engineers had already spent years optimizing.

The same approach helped improve Jalapeño, our first custom inference chip, with gains verified on real silicon.

New evaluations also show our models getting better at certain chip design tasks.

We’re sharing these results and how we’re working with @Synopsys to bring our model capabilities and their trusted EDA design and validation tools to more chip designers.

item.title: @robotaxitracker：Waymo在加州，2026年第三季度：9月份创下纪录，单次行程里程大幅增加——迄今为止最繁忙的月份。9月份无人驾驶行程达1,528,823次，平均每天约51,000次。这打破了5月份的纪录，增长了50%。…
item.description:
Waymo in California, Q3 2026: a record September, and far more miles per ride

- Busiest month yet. September had 1,528,823 driverless rides, about 51,000 a day. That beats May’s record and is up 50% on September 2025. July and August were slower than spring, so the quarter as a whole (4.08M rides) was 3% below Q2. It was still up 53% on a year ago.
- Miles grew much faster than rides. Waymo drove 33.3M miles in Q3, up 18% on Q2 and nearly double a year ago. Most of the extra was empty driving: miles with no ride assigned rose 50% in one quarter. 47.9% of all miles had no rider, up from 41.1%. Rides also got longer, averaging 4.25 miles with a passenger aboard, up from 3.93.
- The reported area more than tripled. The filing lists 6,298 census tracts across 18 counties, up from 1,796 tracts in 5. New counties include San Diego, Orange, Alameda, Contra Costa and Sacramento. Trips per tract are redacted, so this shows the area Waymo reports on, not where rides happened.
- Fewer collisions on more miles. Waymo reported 201 collisions, down from 291, even with 18% more miles. That is 6.0 per million miles, the lowest of the seven quarters CPUC has published in this format. CPUC counts any contact, however minor. Waymo reported 3 serious injuries (2 in Q2) and no fatalities.
- Complaints more than doubled. Complaints rose from 514 to 1,135. Pickup and drop-off complaints went from 79 to 346. That is still about 1 complaint per 3,600 rides.
- Remote help scaled with miles. Stops where Waymo’s remote assistance team helped a car numbered 161,824, about 4 per 100 rides. Per mile the rate was flat, at 4.9 per 1,000 miles in both Q2 and Q3.

item.title: @EpochAIResearch：最强大的语言学习模型（LLM）能在实际工作中与人类匹敌吗？至少在我们Epoch公司所从事的工作类型中，目前还无法做到这一点。我们使用GPT-6.2 Astra和其他最新模型，在Epoch自动化报告（我们的基准测试）上进行了测试。
item.description:
Can the most capable LLMs match humans at real work? Not yet, at least not on the kind of work we do at Epoch.

We tested GPT-6.2 Astra and other recent models on Epoch Automation Reports, our benchmark of open-ended Epoch work tasks, ranging from making Epoch-style diagrams to designing basic research experiments.

An Epoch employee scores the models’ outputs based on our internal quality standards. A score of 100% represents the standard expected of an Epoch employee.

All models failed to meet the Epoch employee standard. GPT-6.2 Astra ranks fourth (averaging 65%), despite sharing the top ECI score of 174 with Fable 5.2.

item.title: @ArtificialAnlys：OpenAI’s release of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol delivers the #2 model in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier @OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra is priced at…
item.description:
OpenAI’s release of GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol delivers the #2 model in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index and most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier

@OpenAI's GPT-6.2 Astra is priced at $8/$40, 20% below GPT-6 Astra, and cached input drops to $0.40 from $1.00 per million tokens. GPT-6.2 Sol pricing is unchanged from GPT-6.1 Sol, at $2/$10 per million input/output tokens.

Key takeaways:
➤ Second in Intelligence Index: OpenAI now trails only Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 in the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. GPT-6.2 Astra jumps 5 points from GPT-6 Astra, overtaking Gemini 4 Carbon (60) and Claude Opus 5.5 (59) at their top effort settings. GPT-6.2 Sol gains 2 points at 57, placing it on par with GPT-6 Astra at ~15% of the Cost per Task.

➤ Occupies most of cost and output token frontiers: OpenAI models now occupy most of the Cost per Task Pareto frontier, sharing the frontier with only Anthropic and Meta. OpenAI also dominates the Output Token per Task Pareto Frontier, with Claude Fable 5.2 being the only model from a non-OpenAI lab appearing on the frontier.

➤ Strengths in science and knowledge: OpenAI performs strongly in both of our key science-focused evaluations, leading Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1, covering agentic scientific research workflows, and placing second only to Claude Fable 5.2 in CritPt v2 (hard subset), covering physics reasoning. GPT-6.2 Astra performs below only Claude Fable 5.2 in factual knowledge as measured by AA-Omniscience v1.1 Accuracy, and in HLE-Diamond, a reasoning and knowledge benchmark.

➤ Leading in 3D and robotics: GPT-6.2 Astra leads AA-3D at 1318, with Claude Fable 5.2 at 1271 and GPT-6.2 Sol at 1259. This benchmark measures how well models build interactive 3D experiences, and is rated by human graders. GPT-6.2 also leads AA-Robotics v0.1, our research preview measuring how well language models can understand, plan, and act in the real world. GPT-6.2 Astra and GPT-6.2 Sol scored 79 and 78 respectively, ahead of Claude Fable 5.2 at 75. Our team is hard at work adding more difficult tasks, as OpenAI and Anthropic models can now perform the majority of basic tasks in this initial research preview.

➤ No improvement in Coding Agent Index: GPT-6.2 Astra is flat with GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.2 Sol loses 3 points relative to GPT-6.1 Sol in the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index (Codex harness at max effort). For Sol, the drop is driven by a 14-point drop in SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, where the model is more likely than its predecessor to omit key facts in its responses. Cost efficiency however does place several effort levels of GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol on the Pareto frontier for Cost per Task.
